title: QuantumCliff healthcare — Efficiency playbook (preview)
body:
Purpose

This is a working preview for QuantumCliff (telehealth workload) — a concise before/after savings analysis applying Redwood Optimize recommendations. The goal: give the customer a clear expected monthly cost delta, recommended config changes, and a prioritized implementation checklist they can action with their engineering team.

Quick summary (one-line)

Baseline estimated monthly inference cost: $54,900. Expected monthly cost after Redwood Optimize recommendations: $20,700 (approx. 62% cost reduction) under the expected scenario.

Customer profile and workload signals

- Customer: QuantumCliff (series B telehealth).
- Primary endpoints: clinical-note generation (free-form), chat triage, and discharge-summary batch jobs.
- Traffic: 750k inference requests / month. Average tokens per request (model-level) ~680 tokens (prompt + completion).
- SLA: p95 latency target for interactive flows <= 800ms. Batch jobs can be up to 6 hours latency.
- Current model footprint: standard Llama-2-70B equivalent (floating point fp16 on GPU), no KV cache enabled for prompt templates, no model quantization, occasional reserved capacity (minimal).

Baseline assumptions (how we computed baseline)

- Request mix: 80% interactive chat/note-gen, 20% end-of-day batch summaries.
- Average prompt length: 220 tokens; average completion: 460 tokens => 680 tokens per request.
- Serving mode: single-token streaming for interactive; batch uses full-sequence generation.
- Throughput profile: uniform during clinic hours (9am–6pm), spiky for after-hours batch windows.
- Baseline per-token compute cost assumed from QuantumCliff's telemetry + Redwood hosted pricing proxy. Baseline monthly cost broken down in the spreadsheet (attached in linked artifacts) — compute + memory + networking + storage overhead.

Key inefficiencies observed

1) No KV/prefix caching for templated prompts (huge reuse in triage flows).
2) Large model (70B) used across both interactive and batch flows; smaller 13B equivalent meets quality threshold on 65% of requests.
3) No quantized serving — running fp16 on high-end GPUs when int8/in4 might be acceptable.
4) Serial single-request execution with little request coalescing during clinic hours.

Redwood Optimize recommendations (high level)

A) Deploy two model tiers and smart routing
- Interactive-critical: keep 13B-quantized (int8) tuned for latency.
- Fallback/High-quality: keep 70B-quantized only for flagged long-form summaries that fail quality thresholds.
- Routing policy: latency-first for triage endpoints, cost-first for batch run.

B) Enable KV/prefix caching for the templated triage sequences
- Cache recent prompt prefixes and KV cache across sessions when user/clinic templates are identical.
- Use TTL 15 minutes for triage context; invalidate on template updates.

C) Quantization profile and kernel selection
- Recommend int8 (GPTQ-style) for 13B and 70B where tolerances allow; fallback to fp16 for non-quantizable ops.
- Adopt mixed-kernel runtime selection for 70B to reduce memory pressure.

D) Batching and request coalescing during clinic hours
- Continuous batching with dynamic target batch sizes (autotune to keep p95 latency <=800ms).
- Leverage small batching window (5–10ms) for interactive flows to raise GPU utilization.

E) Reserved capacity for predictable daytime traffic + burst pool for spikes
- 60% daytime commit, 40% burstable. This reduces unit cost and gives predictable SLAs.

Before / After model (numbers) — expected scenario

Notes on rounding: figures are rounded to nearest $100. All numbers monthly.

- Baseline monthly tokens served: 750,000 requests * 680 tokens = ~510M tokens.
- Baseline monthly inference cost (compute + infra): $54,900.

After applying recommendations (expected):
- Token reduction via caching and prompt truncation: 14% reduction in generated tokens (prefix caching avoids regenerating 14% of tokens on average). => effective tokens = 438M.
- Model swap & quantization unit cost reduction: 13B-int8 unit cost ~45% of 70B-fp16 per-token compute. Combined weighting (60% on 13B, 40% on 70B fallback) => blended per-token compute cost reduction ~56%.
- Intelligent batching & reserved capacity reduces infra overhead by an additional 10%.

Estimated monthly cost after optimizations: $20,700.

Conservative / Aggressive sensitivity scenarios

- Conservative (lower caching, slower quantization adoption): 35% cost reduction -> monthly $35,700.
- Expected (baseline values above): 62% cost reduction -> monthly $20,700.
- Aggressive (high cache hit, full-routed 13B adoption, int4 quant): up to 75% reduction -> monthly $13,700.

Savings timeline and implementation phases (recommended)

Phase 0 — Quick wins (2–3 weeks)
- Enable KV/prefix caching for triage endpoints (engineering + infra). Quick validation: expect 8–12% immediate token reduction.
- Small model A/B test: route 10% of interactive sessions to quantized 13B for quality check.

Phase 1 — Core rollout (1–2 months)
- Expand 13B-int8 to 60% of interactive traffic with auto-fallback on quality metrics.
- Implement continuous batching autotuner in the runtime.
- Commit reserved daytime capacity and configure burst pool.

Phase 2 — Quality & refinement (2–3 months)
- Fine-tune prompt-trimming rules and per-route caching policies.
- Run end-to-end regression tests on clinical note fidelity; adjust model thresholds.

Open questions / risks (items for the PoC)

- Quantization quality: need to validate clinical note fidelity on a curated test-suite (Confluence linked test set). Who ops the evaluation? (Action: Priya to own test-pack run).
- Compliance & audit: KV caching must not persist PHI beyond allowed TTL; audit trail required. Are there existing DLP hooks? (Action: Security sync).
- Latency tradeoffs during heavy clinic-hour bursts — need to ensure batching windows don't violate p95. (Action: SRE to simulate).

Sample tracker columns for the accompanying spreadsheet (so CS + Eng can reproduce numbers)

- route_id, request_type, avg_prompt_tokens, avg_completion_tokens, total_requests_month, baseline_cost_token, optimized_cost_token, cache_hit_rate, %traffic_to_13B, quant_profile, estimated_monthly_cost_baseline, estimated_monthly_cost_optimized, notes

Example line (text)
- triage_v2, interactive, 190, 350, 600000, $0.00011, $0.00005, 0.18, 0.6, int8, $41,400, $15,200, "expected scenario; caching already applied 18%"

Recommended next steps (immediate asks)

1) Client-facing: send this preview + simplified 1-pager to QuantumCliff CSM (Marco to own) — include expected monthly savings and timelines.
2) Engineering: small PoC to enable KV cache and route 10% to 13B-int8. Ticket: JIRA OPT-4821 (priority P2).
3) Security & Compliance: confirm PHI retention limits and logging needs for cache entries.
4) Product: prepare a short eval rubric (5–10 test prompts) to evaluate generative quality delta between 70B-fp16 and 13B-int8.

Appendix: quick math notes (raw)

- Baseline tokens = 750k * 680 = 510,000,000 tokens/month.
- Cache savings (expected) 14% => tokens avoided ~71.4M; effective tokens 438.6M.
- Blended per-token compute cost baseline assumed $0.0001077/token (derived from telemetry and pricing proxy) => baseline compute cost ~ $54,970 ~ $54,900 (rounded).
- Post-optimization blended per-token cost ~ $0.0000472 => optimized compute cost ~ $20,700.

Notes to reviewer

- This doc is intentionally concise — the linked spreadsheet contains the cell-level model and per-route breakout. Please add comments in-line for any number you disagree with.
- Prioritize quick cache PoC and 10% model-swap A/B, as these unlock the majority of near-term savings.

Draft history

- 2025-11-10: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-11-18: added sensitivity scenarios (Marco)
- 2026-01-04: inserted implementation phases (Priya)
- 2026-03-01: updated numbers after internal runtime benchmarking (Samir)

Unresolved: who at QuantumCliff is owning the PoC (request CSM confirmation).
